judgment.rationale: A maintainer reproduced Win+M and the reporter supplied diagnostics plus additional concrete cases. The pattern points to physical and remapped modifier state being mixed when OS-level shortcuts are evaluated.
evidence: Maintainer reproduced Alt(left)→Win(left) causing physical Alt+M not to invoke Win+M, while a direct Alt+M→Win+M shortcut works.
Win+W becomes Game Bar behavior and pen-generated Win+F18–F20 are observed as Alt after the swap.
Current Keyboard Manager has special Win-key and lower-level modifier reset paths, confirming modifier identity is handled asymmetrically.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce on current code and design explicit physical-to-logical modifier state for single-key swaps across OS and synthetic-device input.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked fix establishes current coverage; the reproduced modifier-composition failure supports a focused plan.

proposed_fixes.title: Separate physical modifier identity from remapped logical modifier state
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Bidirectional Win/Alt single-key remaps can suppress or restore physical modifier events in an order that leaves Windows shell shortcut detection seeing the original modifier for some synthetic or system-handled chords.
plan: Add engine tests for simultaneous Win→Alt and Alt→Win mappings with M, W, and F18–F20 action keys.
Track the logical modifier produced by each physical modifier until its matching key-up, including injected device shortcuts.
Apply consistent Win-specific dummy/suppression handling without rewriting unrelated modifier state.
verification: Run KeyboardManagerEngine tests for swapped modifiers and direct shortcut remaps.
Verify physical Alt+M invokes Win+M and physical Win+W behaves as Alt+W under the configured swap.
Verify pen-generated Win+F18–F20 are transformed consistently and all modifiers release.

confidence.rationale: The behavior is reproducible and the state boundary is clear, but current code has changed substantially since 0.58 and requires a fresh engine-level reproduction.

issue_context.summary: Swapping left Win and left Alt as single-key remaps breaks some Windows-key combinations and causes synthetic device shortcuts such as pen Win+F18–F20 to be observed as Alt combinations.
known_information: The reporter uses a Mac-layout Logitech keyboard and swaps Win and Alt.
A maintainer reproduced the Win+M failure.
A direct shortcut remap works around Win+M, and explicit Alt+F18–F20 remaps work around pen shortcuts.
A bug report archive was attached in 2022.
inferences: Single-key remap state is not consistently applied to shell-consumed or device-generated chords.
issue_context.analysis: The direct shortcut workaround shows the target chord can be injected; the defect is in composing other keys with two simultaneously swapped modifiers.
initial_investigation: Read the full body and seven comments through 2022-10-24T21:30:26Z.
Reviewed current KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp modifier special cases and reset paths.
No linked fix or duplicate is present in the timeline, and the issue remains labeled Status-Reproducible.

actions.label: Reproduce swapped Win and Alt chords

reproduce.title: Verify logical modifier composition
prerequisites: Configure Win(left) → Alt(left) and Alt(left) → Win(left)
Open ordinary desktop windows; optionally connect a pen that emits Win+F18–F20
steps: Press physical Alt(left)+M and verify Windows minimizes all windows.
Press physical Win(left)+W and record the logical shortcut observed.
If available, trigger pen F18–F20 shortcuts and inspect emitted modifiers.
Release all keys and verify no modifier remains logically pressed.
reproduce.expected_result: Every chord uses the remapped logical modifier consistently and key-up restores neutral state.
